    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    Architecture
    The instruction set an ArduinoCore runs generated code on, which picks the code generator: the UNO R4's Cortex-M4 and the UNO Q's Cortex-M33 share one Thumb-2 backend, the UNO WiFi Rev2's ATmega4809 has its own AVR one, and the Nano ESP32's ESP32-S3 an Xtensa one.
    ArduinoCore
    The Arduino core a Board is built with.
    ArduinoNano
    The Arduino Nano ESP32's features: its Gpio pins, primary I2c bus, USB Mouse, onboard Wifi, Clock, board identity (BoardModel), and arena and flash figures (BoardMemory).
    ArduinoNanoEsp32Board
    Selects the Arduino Nano ESP32 as @Board's target: Juno programs run on its ESP32-S3, a dual-core Xtensa LX7, under Arduino's arduino:esp32 core.
    ArduinoNanoEsp32Image
    Generated from arduino-nano-esp32.png, rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise, then displayed rotated 180 degrees.
    ArduinoUno
    The Arduino UNO board's microcontroller unit (MCU): its Gpio pins, its I2c bus, its USB Mouse, its built-in LedMatrix, its onboard Wifi, its Clock, which board it is (BoardModel) and its arena and flash figures (BoardMemory).
    ArduinoUnoBoardImage
    Generated by CoverImageGenerator from 2.png, rotated 90 degrees clockwise; do not edit by hand.
    ArduinoUnoQBoard
    Selects the Arduino UNO Q as @Board's target: Juno programs run on its STM32U585 microcontroller (Cortex-M33) under Arduino's Zephyr core.
    ArduinoUnoR3Board
    Selects the classic Arduino UNO R3 as @Board's target: Juno programs run on its ATmega328P, an 8-bit AVR with 2 KB SRAM and 32 KB flash, under Arduino's arduino:avr core.
    ArduinoUnoR3WiFiRev2Board
    Selects the Arduino UNO WiFi Rev2 as @Board's target: Juno programs run on its ATmega4809, an 8-bit megaAVR (6 KB SRAM, 48 KB flash), under Arduino's arduino:megaavr core, with Wi-Fi through the u-blox NINA-W102 module and the WiFiNINA library.
    ArduinoUnoR4WiFiBoard
    Selects the Arduino UNO R4 WiFi as @Board's target; has the onboard 12x8 LED matrix.
    ArduinoWifiShield
    The retired Arduino WiFi Shield, the UNO R3's only way onto a Wi-Fi network: the R3 has no radio of its own, so ArduinoUno.getWifi() is rejected there and the program takes its Wifi from this shield instead.
    ArrayDeclaration
    One local array a method declares via IrInstruction.NewArray, hoisted to the top of the function.
    ArrayElementType
    The element type of a Juno-supported array.
    AsmBackend
    Generates assembly and its runtime shim for one instruction-set architecture.
    AsmEmitter
    The instruction-level building blocks every lowering shares: moving words between registers and a method's fixed stack slots (see FrameLayout), materializing immediates and string-literal addresses, calling extern "C" runtime-shim functions under AAPCS, and minting unique local labels.
    AtomicSupport
    The deliberately small java.util.concurrent.atomic subset lowered by Juno: AtomicInteger, AtomicBoolean and AtomicLong, each an arena cell whose operations run in the runtime, where the preemptive scheduler never interrupts them halfway.
    Audio
    The Cardputer's built-in speaker.
    AvrAsmBackend
    Emits GNU AVR assembly (avrxmega3, the UNO WiFi Rev2's ATmega4809) straight from Juno IR — the 8-bit counterpart of Thumb2AsmBackend, with the same storage model: every IR value and JVM local lives in a fixed stack slot (see FrameLayout.packed(IrMethod)) and registers are only scratch within one instruction, so a method can never run out of registers.
    AvrRuntimeShim
    Generates the C++ runtime shim of an AVR program, the counterpart of RuntimeShim.
    AvrShimThunks
    Generates the C++ thunks AVR code calls the runtime shim through. avr-gcc passes a const char* in two registers, an int32_t in four and a uint8_t in one, so assembly that only knows Java words cannot call a C function directly without knowing its parameter types.
    BasicBlock
    A maximal run of instructions with one entry point (start) and one exit (terminator).
    Battery
    Battery readings exposed by a board.
    BaudRate
    Common baud rates exposed as named values by Juno's USB serial API.
    BigNumberMethods
    The java.math subset: BigInteger, BigDecimal and MathContext.
    BigNumberSupport
    Closed-world plumbing for the java.math subset: BigInteger, BigDecimal and MathContext are one-word handles to immutable arena blocks, and RoundingMode is its ordinal.
    BigNumberSupport.Constant
    A static final field Juno materializes itself: a constructed value or a plain ordinal.
    BinaryOp
    A binary arithmetic or bitwise operation, with Java int (32-bit two's complement) semantics.
    BlockMerging
    Joins a block that ends in a Jump with its target when it is that target's only way in, so straight-line code (an inlined body and its continuation, say) is one block with no branch between the halves.

    Declares which Arduino board(s) a Juno program targets, e.g.

    ConstantTables
    Read-only lookup tables kept in flash (.rodata) instead of the 8 KiB arena: a static final one-dimensional primitive array whose <clinit> initializer is all compile-time constants (static final short[] T = {1, 2, 3};) and which every reachable method only ever reads as T[i] or T.length.
    ConstantTables.RamFallback
    A static final constant-initialized array that has to stay in the arena, and why.
    ConstantTables.Table
    One flash-resident table: element values as raw bits, sign-extended for the integer types.
    ControlFlowGraph
    The basic blocks of one method, in offset order, with branch targets resolved into block-to-block edges.
    ControlFlowGraph
    The control-flow graph of one IrMethod, shared by the data-flow passes: every block's successors and predecessors (by block start), a reverse postorder from the entry block, and the dominator tree.
    ControlFlowGraphBuilder
    Partitions a method's decoded instructions into BasicBlocks and resolves every branch target into a CFG edge, replacing byte-offset jumps with an explicit block graph.
    CopyPropagation
    Eliminates a IrInstruction.LoadLocal when preceding stores determine the slot's value.
    CoreRuntime
    Everything the generated code needs to know about the ArduinoCore it links against: the symbols Delay lowers to and the runtime shim's yield()/delay glue.
    CoreRuntime.BleNames
    The BLE central names the LEGO Powered UP runtime is written against: ArduinoBLE's device, characteristic and scanner object.
    CoreRuntimes
    The one place that names a CoreRuntime implementation: each ArduinoCore maps to exactly one.
    DataLoggerShield
    The AZDelivery Data Logger Module Data Recorder Shield: an SD card socket on the UNO's SPI pins, chip select on D10 (MOSI D11, MISO D12, SCK D13), plus a DS1307 real-time clock that this class does not drive.
    DeadBlockElimination
    Removes basic blocks unreachable from a method's entry block.
    DeadLocalStoreElimination
    Removes stores to JVM/synthetic local slots that no later load can read.
    DeadValueElimination
    Removes instructions that only compute a value nothing reads: constants, local and static loads, field loads, integer arithmetic other than division and remainder (which can panic on zero), comparisons and conversions.

    Timing operations recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno.

    NativeBoardMemory
    The board's BoardMemory: each method is an intrinsic the compiler lowers to its runtime shim, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeBoardModel
    The board's BoardModel: each method is an intrinsic the compiler folds to a constant for the target board, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeClock
    The board's Clock: each method is a clock intrinsic the compiler lowers to the Arduino core call, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeDigitalOutput
    The board's DigitalOutput factory: NativeDigitalOutput.of(int) is a GPIO intrinsic the compiler lowers to a pin mode and returns the pin number as the handle.
    NativeDisplay
    The M5Stack Cardputer's Display, implemented by compiler intrinsics over M5StackCardputer.Display.
    NativeGpio
    The board's Gpio: each method is a GPIO intrinsic the compiler lowers to the Arduino core call, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeI2c
    The board's I2c: each method is an I2C intrinsic the compiler lowers to the core-bundled Wire library, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeKeyboard
    The M5Stack Cardputer's Keyboard, implemented by compiler intrinsics over M5StackCardputer.Keyboard.
    NativeLedMatrix
    The board's LedMatrix: each method is an LED matrix intrinsic the compiler lowers to the Arduino_LED_Matrix library, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeMouse
    The board's Mouse: each method is a USB HID intrinsic the compiler lowers to the Arduino Mouse library (the core's USBHIDMouse on ESP32-S3 boards), so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeSdCard
    The card in a shield's SD socket: each method but NativeSdCard.begin() is an SD intrinsic the compiler lowers to the SdFat library, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.
    NativeWifi
    The board's Wifi: each method is a Wi-Fi intrinsic the compiler lowers to the board's networking library, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM.

    What a View uses to hand over control.

    The JVM opcodes by their specification names (JVMS chapter 6), so code that inspects bytecode reads opcode == INVOKESTATIC rather than opcode == 184.

    ParallelBusRuntime
    The shim half of ParallelBus.

    Mutable, allocation-free planar pose for a differential-drive robot.

    A LEGO Powered Up hub (City Hub 88009, Technic Hub 88012, BOOST Move Hub 88006, DUPLO Train Hub, ...) controlled over Bluetooth Low Energy, recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno and backed by the Arduino ArduinoBLE library (arduino-cli lib install ArduinoBLE).
    PoweredUpPort
    The Powered Up hub intrinsics as an interface: NativePoweredUpPort drives the real hub on the board, and a mock or fake takes its place in a unit test through PoweredUpHubRemote(PoweredUpPort, io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.time.Clock).
    PowerFunctionsRemote
    A LEGO Power Functions infrared remote (8885), which drives the motors, lights and servos plugged into an IR Receiver (8884) set to one of its four channels.
    Program
    classes is every class loaded from the classpath (not just reachable methods' owners) — needed so that lowering can resolve a getstatic on an enum constant field to its ordinal, since the field's owner class may differ from the reachable method's own owner and is otherwise never visited (its <clinit>/<init>/values()/etc. are deliberately never added to methods).
    ProgramLayout
    Whole-program storage decisions made before any code is emitted: arena object sizes and field offsets, mutable static fields' .bss symbols, and the .rodata symbols of string literals and compiler-generated constant int arrays — plus the data sections holding them.
    ProgramLayout.DataDirectives
    The assembler directives a data section is written with: word emits 32-bit values (ARM's .word; AVR's .word is 16-bit, so it uses .long), align 4-byte-aligns, and bss switches to the zero-initialized section (AVR's assembler has no .bss shorthand).
    PwmServoShield
    The "16 x 12-bit PWM & Servo Shield": an NXP PCA9685 that generates sixteen servo signals on its own, driven over I2C as plain Java on top of I2c (so it needs no Arduino library).
    Random
    Pseudorandom-number operations backed by Arduino's random generator.
    RandomAccessFileMethods
    The read-only java.io.RandomAccessFile subset, backed by the SD card's open-file table: a file opened with mode "r" by a compile-time literal path, then seek/getFilePointer/length, single-byte and buffer reads, skipBytes and close.

    An RCX brick's own View, Prgm and Run buttons, from RemoteRcx.getButtons().
    RcxChannelAudio
    A zero-allocation channel-aware speaker for Juno's channelized RCX firmware.
    RcxFirmware
    Loads firmware into an RCX brick over infrared, as the LEGO IR tower does: the brick's boot ROM answers these four commands even when it has no firmware, which is the state it is in after its batteries were out (the display then shows program 0).
    RcxLcd
    An RCX brick's display, from RemoteRcx.getLcd().
    RcxLight
    A lamp connected to one of an RCX brick's motor outputs for tone activity indication.
    RcxLightSensor
    A light sensor plugged into an RCX input, e.g.
    RcxLink
    The RCX infrared framing: a message is 55 FF 00 followed by the opcode, its arguments and a checksum, each byte followed by its complement.
    RcxMotor
    One or more of an RCX brick's outputs, driven with direct commands over infrared: get them from RemoteRcx.getMotorA(), RemoteRcx.getMotorB() and RemoteRcx.getMotorC(), and combine them with RcxMotor.and(RcxMotor) so that several outputs start and stop in the same command, e.g. the two sides of a vehicle.
    RcxRotationSensor
    A rotation sensor plugged into an RCX input, e.g.
    RcxSensor
    One of an RCX brick's three sensor inputs, as LeJOS's SensorPort: get it from RemoteRcx.getSensor1(), RemoteRcx.getSensor2() or RemoteRcx.getSensor3() and hand it to the sensor plugged into it, an RcxTouchSensor, RcxLightSensor, RcxTemperatureSensor or RcxRotationSensor, created once, at startup.
    RcxTemperatureSensor
    A temperature sensor plugged into an RCX input, e.g.
    RcxTouchSensor
    A touch sensor plugged into an RCX input, e.g.
    RegulatedMotor
    A motor with encoder feedback and closed-loop speed/position control.
    RemoteRcx
    A LEGO Mindstorms RCX brick reached over infrared, in the manner of LeJOS's RemoteNXT: create it once, at startup, with the infrared RcxLink and the pins of the IR receiver module and the IR LED, call RemoteRcx.begin(), and get the brick's parts from it — its motors (RemoteRcx.getMotorA(), RemoteRcx.getMotorB(), RemoteRcx.getMotorC()), its sensor inputs (RemoteRcx.getSensor1(), RemoteRcx.getSensor2(), RemoteRcx.getSensor3()), its display (RemoteRcx.getLcd()), its speaker (RemoteRcx.getAudio()), its batteries (RemoteRcx.getBattery()) and its firmware loader (RemoteRcx.getFirmware()).
    RiskSeverity
    Severity of a runtime-risk diagnostic emitted after IR optimization.
    RuntimeConfig
    The capacities of the generated runtime: how much RAM the arena and the task stacks take.
    RuntimeEntryPoints
    What every backend needs to know about the concurrency runtime: the generated functions the shim calls back into, and whether a program needs the preemptive scheduler at all.
    RuntimeLimits
    Runtime constants shared by analysis and the current UNO R4 backend.
    RuntimeRisk
    One stable, machine-readable runtime-risk finding.
    RuntimeRiskAnalyzer
    Conservative resource and runtime-risk analysis over the optimized closed-world IR.
    RuntimeRiskReport
    Resource estimates and runtime-risk findings for one closed-world compilation.
    RuntimeRiskReportFormatter
    Renders a RuntimeRiskReport as human-readable lines, shared by the CLI and the Maven plugin.
    RuntimeShim
    Generates the extern "C" C++ runtime shim compiled alongside the generated assembly: wrappers around things the assembly can't call directly — the arena allocator/panic handler and ArduinoLEDMatrix (a C++-only object with inline-only methods and private timer/frame state — no stable symbol to call without knowing its private layout) — plus every optional helper block (ShimLibraries, NetworkShimLibraries) and library include the lowered program's ShimFeatures call for.
    RuntimeSource
    The C++ fragments the runtime shim is assembled from, kept as real source files under src/main/resources/runtime rather than Java strings: common/ for every board, thumb2//avr/ for one instruction set, and renesas//zephyr//megaavr/ for one ArduinoCore.
    ScalarReplacement
    Removes an allocation whose object never escapes the method, keeping its fields in local slots instead of the arena: no juno_alloc, no garbage for the collector, and field accesses that copy propagation and constant folding can see through.
    ScopedValueSupport
    Closed-world plumbing for the java.lang.ScopedValue subset (JDK 25, final API).
    SdCard
    Access to an SPI SD card, backed by the Arduino SdFat library with long-file-name support enabled.
    Serial
    USB serial output recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno.
    Servo
    A zero-cost servo motor handle for a standard 3-wire hobby servo (signal, power, ground), backed by the Arduino Servo library.
    ShimFeature
    An optional part of the generated runtime shim, recorded while lowering the program's IR and consulted by
    invalid reference 
    RuntimeShim
    so each include and helper block is emitted only when some generated code actually calls into it.
    ShimLibraries
    Source text of the runtime shim's optional, self-contained C++ helper blocks for peripherals, storage, strings, exceptions and 64-bit/floating-point arithmetic — each appended by RuntimeShim only when the lowered program actually calls into it.
    SketchWrapper
    The .ino file that turns generated assembly into an Arduino sketch: its setup() calls the program's entry point, which never returns, so loop() stays empty.
    Smtp
    A minimal SMTP client recognized as a compiler intrinsic by Juno.
    SntpClock
    The SNTP server behind the internet-backed LocalDateTime.now() intrinsic, which synchronizes UTC over one UDP exchange on its own socket (separate from Udp's) and then advances it with the board's millisecond counter.
    SoftFloatRuntime
    Java's float and double in software, for an architecture whose C double is narrower than IEEE binary64 (avr-gcc's is 32 bits).
    StackFrameSizing
    Authoritative target-backend stack sizing shared with static runtime-risk analysis.
    StringConcatResolver
    Validates and decodes the bounded subset of javac's string-concatenation bootstrap protocol.
    StringConcatSite
    A validated StringConcatFactory.makeConcatWithConstants call site.
    StringConcatSite.ArgumentPart
     
    StringConcatSite.LiteralPart
     
    StringConcatSite.Part
    One literal fragment or dynamic argument in the bootstrap recipe.
    StructuredTaskSupport
    Closed-world plumbing for Juno's JDK 27 preview StructuredTaskScope subset.
    SupportedJdkMethods
    Small JDK bytecode idioms Juno lowers without linking their JDK implementations.
    Task
    Background work a ViewRouter advances a little every frame, before the active view renders: the single-threaded alternative to a background thread, for a board whose RAM has no room for a thread stack.
    Tcp
    Allocation-free TCP transport recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno.
    Terminator
    Where control flow goes after the last instruction of a BasicBlock.
    Terminator.Branch
    A conditional branch: control goes to trueTarget or falls through to falseTarget.
    Terminator.Fallthrough
    Falls into the next block without an explicit branch instruction.
    Terminator.Jump
    Unconditional goto.
    Terminator.Return
    A supported JVM return opcode, or the implicit return past the last instruction of a method.
    Terminator.Switch
     
    Terminator.Throw
    athrow: control continues at one of handlers — the distinct handler offsets whose exception-table ranges cover the throw, in matching order — or leaves the method when none catches it.
    TftTouchShield
    Driver for the ELEGOO 2.8" TFT touch screen shield ("Pantalla Táctil TFT de 2,8 pulgadas"): a 240x320 ILI9341 display on an 8-bit parallel bus, a 4-wire resistive touch panel, and a microSD socket, wired for the shield's standard UNO pinout as used by ELEGOO's Elegoo_TFTLCD and TouchScreen libraries.
    ThreadRuntime
    The C++ source of the java.lang.Thread runtime in the generated shim: threads, each on a stack of its own, time-sliced by the scheduler (ThreadRuntime.scheduler(boolean, boolean, int, String, String, boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean, int, int)) every JUNO_TIME_SLICE_MILLIS.
    ThreadSupport
    The closed-world plumbing behind java.lang.Thread: a started thread runs its Runnable on a stack of its own, entered from the runtime shim, so the linker registers one synthetic Runnable.run() call site that resolves against every reachable Runnable (classes and lambdas) and the lowering turns it into the generated thread entry function.
    ThrowableTypes
    The closed-world exception hierarchy: a fixed set of built-in JDK throwables (which Juno models itself, since their class files are never on the classpath) plus any program class whose superclass chain reaches one of them.
    Thumb2AsmBackend
    Emits GNU ARM Thumb-2 assembly straight from Juno IR, restricted to instructions common to the UNO R4's Cortex-M4 and the UNO Q's Cortex-M33, so one code generator serves every board; per-core runtime differences live in CoreRuntime.
    Udp
    Allocation-free UDP transport recognized as compiler intrinsics by Juno.
    UnaryOp
    A single-operand operation: arithmetic negation or a narrowing conversion.
    UnoGeneration
    The UNO generation a Board belongs to: the answer to io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.BoardModel's isR3()/isR4()/isQ().
    UuidCodec
    Converts UUID values to and from their 16-byte, most-significant-byte-first network representation.
    UuidMethods
    The supported java.util.UUID methods.
    UuidSupport
    Closed-world plumbing for UUID values represented by one-word handles to immutable arena blocks.
    Value
    A typed symbolic virtual register: one value, produced by exactly one IrInstruction.
    View
    One screen of a multi-view program.
    ViewRouter
    The controller of a multi-view TFT program: it owns the views, runs the frame loop and switches the active view when a view asks through Navigator.
    Watchdog
    Enables the target's hardware watchdog timer on @Watchdog's entry-point class.
    WatchdogRuntime
    Core-specific source fragments for one hardware-watchdog configuration.
    Wifi
    Wi-Fi connection control.
    WifiProvisioner
    Wi-Fi provisioning without baking credentials into the firmware, written in plain Java on top of ArduinoUno.getWifi() and HttpServer (it adds no intrinsics, and costs nothing in a program that does not call it).
    WordSource
    One argument word of a call: Juno's calling convention passes every argument as 32-bit words, in order.
    WordSource.FromValue
     
    WordSource.FromValueHigh
     
    WordSource.FromValueLow
     
    WordSource.Immediate
     
    WordSource.StringAddress
     
    XtensaAsmBackend
    Emits GNU Xtensa assembly (the Nano ESP32's ESP32-S3, an LX7 core) straight from Juno IR, with the storage model of Thumb2AsmBackend: every IR value and JVM local lives in a fixed stack slot (see FrameLayout.packed(IrMethod)) and registers are only scratch within one instruction.
